target_customer: Large pharma and longevity companies as eventual partners or acquirers; patients with age-related diseases long term
problem: Senescent cells drive tissue aging and age-related diseases such as lung fibrosis and osteoarthritis; the company aimed to block senescence with small molecules called senoblockers.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing small-molecule therapeutics, monetized by licensing or exit

founders.name: Maddalena Adorno
founders.background_notes: Sources say she developed the senoblocker concept at Stanford before the spinout. Degrees not found in a source opened.

founders.name: Benedetta di Robilant
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder on the YC page. Background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Discovering small molecules that block cellular senescence is research-grade drug discovery requiring wet labs, DNA-encoded library screening and years of preclinical work.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary compounds and Stanford-derived science could be patented, but the company stayed preclinical with no clinical proof.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Altos Labs acquired the company in May 2025, terms undisclosed.

market_need_then: Aging biology and senolytics drew rising investor interest around 2018, with Unity Biotechnology listing publicly that year, but no senescence drug was approved.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found; a scientific B2B name with little public identity. Site now redirects to the acquirer.

outcome_analysis: Dorian was a Stanford spinout developing senoblocker small molecules for age-related disease and stayed preclinical. Altos Labs acquired it in May 2025 with undisclosed terms. One longevity outlet speculated the deal may have been an acquihire given weak biotech fundraising, but no source confirms the economics, so the outcome quality is unknown.
notes: Website redirects to altoslabs.com. Seed amount not public; CB Insights total of $290K and seedtable investor list (YC, Longevity Fund, StartX, Pacific 8, Blumberg) are single aggregator figures, unverified. Dated senolytic competitor sources near 2018 not found, so the list is empty; Unity Biotechnology (founded 2011) existed but source dates are later. Several aggregator rows for other companies named Dorian were ignored. Acquisition stage and terms not stated by sources.
